---
type: Identity Profile
title: "Runtime Contract"
description: "The load order for every writing job, and the checks that run after."
created: 2026-08-22
updated: 2026-09-25
---

# Runtime Contract

> **Purpose:** This file says which rules load, in what order, and which checks run at the end.
> It is the only file that answers "what was applied to this draft". Read it first, every time.
> Adapted from the runtime contract in [Deupaxx/EveryDay-Writer](https://github.com/Deupaxx/EveryDay-Writer).
> The architecture is theirs. The rules and the voice are mine.

## Always loaded

Six files load for every piece of writing, on every channel, in this order.

1. `DIGITAL TWIN/core/runtime-contract.md`, this file. The load order and the checks.
2. `DIGITAL TWIN/core/pattern-rules.md`. The failure patterns a regex cannot see.
3. `DIGITAL TWIN/core/write-simply.md`. The plain style, and the test for whether the ideas are right.
4. `DIGITAL TWIN/World.md`. The villain, the vision, and what the piece is for.
5. `DIGITAL TWIN/core/net-new-value.md`. The bar the insight clears before a word is drafted.
6. `DIGITAL TWIN/Voice.md`. How the writing sounds.

Files 2 and 3 are a pair. The pattern rules say what to remove, and `write-simply.md` says what to
aim for, so a draft that only obeys the first one reads stripped.

`World.md` decides what the piece argues and `Voice.md` decides how it sounds, so the two never
collide. Name the skill-tree node before you draft a line. A piece that advances no node is an
idea, so send it back to `SUBSTACK/0_IDEAS/`.

`net-new-value.md` is the guiding principle for all content, on every channel. Write the core
insight as one sentence and name its box before you draft. Only box 4 ships: non-obvious to the
reader and tactical enough to use today. A piece outside box 4 gets one upgrade, then goes back to
the idea bank.

`SCRIPTS/slop/slop_rules.py` holds the banned words, phrases and punctuation. `DIGITAL TWIN/rules/`
holds the prose rules, one file each. The `core` rules load into every session through the generated
block in `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`, so you never copy them into another file.

The `craft` rules load for every writing job. Run this once per session before the first draft:

```bash
python SCRIPTS/slop/rules_prompt.py --profile craft
```

## Loaded on demand

One more file loads, chosen by the job. Never load two.

| The job | Load this |
|---|---|
| A Substack article, an essay, a long piece | `DIGITAL TWIN/Long-Form Writing Rules.md` |
| A tutorial, a how-to, a README, developer docs | `DIGITAL TWIN/Technical Writing Style Guide.md` |
| A LinkedIn post, a Note, a tweet, a caption | nothing extra. The channel skill carries it |

`DIGITAL TWIN/AI Writing Policy.md` outranks all of the above and it changes rarely, so read it
when you start a writing session and not once per draft.

## Then the channel skill

The skill carries the shape of the channel and nothing else. It never restates a banned word, a
voice rule or a craft rule, because a copy goes stale and then two files disagree.

| Channel | Skill |
|---|---|
| LinkedIn post | `.claude/skills/write-linkedin-posts/SKILL.md` |
| X post or thread | `.claude/skills/banger-tweets/SKILL.md` |
| Substack Note | `.claude/skills/substack-notes/SKILL.md` |
| Substack article | `.claude/skills/substack-writer/SKILL.md` |
| Reddit post | none. `SOCIALS/Reddit/README.md` is the channel spec |
| Landing page or sales email | `.claude/skills/write-sales-copy/SKILL.md` |
| A stuck idea with no shape yet | `.claude/skills/write-outline/SKILL.md` |
| An existing draft that reads like AI | `.claude/skills/deslop-audit/SKILL.md` |

## Precedence, higher wins

Four layers can disagree. Resolve upward.

1. The banned lists in `slop_rules.py` and the patterns in `core/pattern-rules.md`.
2. The channel skill.
3. `DIGITAL TWIN/Voice.md`.
4. A sample Atharva pastes in the current session.

A sample beats the profile. The profile beats the skill. Two rules never override anything above
them. The fabrication rule below, and the five principles in `AI Writing Policy.md`.

## The fabrication rule

Add no fact that Atharva did not supply. That covers a name, a number, a date, a statistic, a
quote, a source, an event and a client. This rule bites hardest on a rewrite, because the fix for
a vague sentence looks like a specific sentence, and the specifics are not yours to invent.

You have three legal moves when a sentence needs a real detail.

1. Ask him for it.
2. Mark the gap in visible brackets, such as `[the real number]`. Brackets cannot ship by accident.
3. Drop the claim to the level the evidence supports, or cut it.

An invented specific that reads well is a worse defect than the vague sentence it replaced. A
reader cannot catch it.

## The two-pass loop

Never hand over a first draft.

**Pass 1.** Write it. Do not judge while you write.

**Pass 2.** Read it cold and answer five questions for yourself, in writing. Do not print the
answers unless he asks.

1. If a reader called this AI, which exact sentence would they point at?
2. Does the draft carry a fact, a name, a number or a source that he did not give me?
3. Which sentence is the weakest, and does the piece rest on it?
4. Which sentence reads worst, and is the idea under it wrong rather than the wording?
5. Is the core insight still box 4 in `core/net-new-value.md`, or did the draft sand it down to box 2?

**Pass 3.** Fix what the answers found. Then run the checks.

## Announce the load order

Render this panel above every draft. Do not type it by hand.

```bash
python SCRIPTS/loadorder/block.py --skill <channel skill> --file "<path>"     --node "<the skill-tree node this piece advances>"     --topic "<the idea, for the pillar check>"     --season "<NN beat N, or none>" --format "<number and name, or n/a>"     --insight "<the box 4 insight, one sentence>"
```

`--glob "<pattern>"` replaces `--file` for a batch, and reports the worst result
across the set. `--plain` drops to ASCII. `--technical` swaps the on-demand file
for the Technical Writing Style Guide. The script exits 1 when any measured check
failed, so a caller can gate on it.

```
╭─ LOAD ORDER ─────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
│ ✓ 1  core/runtime-contract              always               │
│ ✓ 2  core/pattern-rules                 always               │
│ ✓ 3  core/write-simply                  always               │
│ ✓ 4  World.md                           always               │
│ ✓ 5  core/net-new-value                 always               │
│ ✓ 6  Voice.md                           always               │
│ ✓ 7  Long-Form Writing Rules.md         on demand            │
│ ✓ 8  skill:substack-writer              channel              │
├─ WORLD ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ villain  rented work                                         │
│ node     builds a gate that refuses bad work                 │
│ season   01 beat 3      format  05 Contrarian Take           │
│ insight  a hook that returns decision: block stops the save  │
├─ CHECKS, measured ───────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ ✓ pillar      ON (AI)                                        │
│ ✓ slop        CRIT 0                                         │
│ ✓ clarity     CRIT 0                                         │
│ ✓ craft       0                                              │
│ ✓ seo         CRIT 0                                         │
╰──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
```

The two halves carry different weight, and the difference is the point.

**The top half is declared.** You state the node, the season and the box 4 insight. The chain itself
comes from the channel table inside the script, so it cannot drift from this file.

**The bottom half is measured.** The script runs each scorer and prints what it
returned. A tick means a check ran and passed. A cross means it ran and failed. A
dot means the scorer could not run, which never reads as a pass.

That split is why the panel replaced the four hand-typed lines it used to be. A
typed line could claim `slop CRIT 0` for a check nobody ran, which is the blind
spot this contract exists to close. A rendered line cannot.

A missing panel means the chain was skipped.

## The checks, in this order

Run them in order. A later check on a draft that fails an earlier one wastes both your time and his.

| Order | Command | Bar |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | Name the box in `core/net-new-value.md` for the one-sentence insight | Box 4. Every channel |
| 0b | The opening gate in `LIBRARY/Resources/Post Uniqueness Check.md` | The top-ranked of 5 openings ships, and no hook is a question. LinkedIn, X, Notes |
| 1 | `python SCRIPTS/pillars/pillars.py --text "<the idea>"` | ON, or an honest BEND |
| 2 | `python SCRIPTS/substack/overlap.py check "<the idea>"` | WRITE. Articles only |
| 3 | `python SCRIPTS/slop/score.py "<file>"` | CRIT reaches 0 |
| 4 | `python SCRIPTS/clarity/score.py "<file>"` | CRIT reaches 0. Every channel |
| 5 | `python SCRIPTS/socials/li_format.py "<file>"` | CRIT reaches 0. LinkedIn only |
| 6 | `python SCRIPTS/substack/craft.py "<file>"` | 0. Articles only |
| 7 | `python SCRIPTS/seo/score.py "<file>" --write` | 0. Articles only |
| 8 | `python SCRIPTS/socials/coverage.py` | no `source_blog` warning. Social files only |
| 9 | `python SCRIPTS/review/build.py` | the desk carries it. Every draft is on it, nothing to stamp |

Rows 4, 5 and 6 were missing from this table until 2026-09-04. All three existed
and two of them already blocked a commit, so the table was the only place that
disagreed. A check absent from this file gets skipped by anyone who trusts it,
which is the whole reason the file exists. Add a row here in the same commit
that adds a scorer.

Checks 0, 0b, 1 and 2 run before you draft. Checks 3 to 9 run after. Skip a row only when the row says
so, and say in the announcement block which rows you skipped.

MED and LOW findings from the scorer are advisory. On short-form, ignore its flow, paragraph and
fragment findings, because those rules were written for long-form.

## Related

- [AI Writing Policy](../AI%20Writing%20Policy.md), the top directive, above this file
- [Pattern rules](./pattern-rules.md), the second always-loaded file
- [Write Simply](./write-simply.md), the third always-loaded file, the plain style and its test
- [World](../World.md), the villain, the vision and the skill tree
- [Net New Value](./net-new-value.md), the fifth always-loaded file, the bar every insight clears
- [Voice](../Voice.md), how the writing sounds
- [Season 01](../../SUBSTACK/GROWTH%20STRATEGY/Season%2001%20-%20The%20Owned%20System.md), the current 13 weeks
- [Content Pillars](../Content%20Pillars.md), what is allowed on the social channels

49:DIGITAL TWIN/        ← My identity files: About, Voice, Audience, Goals, Principles, Experience, Socials.
64:SOCIALS/             ← Output factory for all social channels.
66:  Tweets/            ← _IDEAS/ bank, tweet_[Title].md drafted, POSTED/ live.
87:                       Never use `substack.py update` for links, use `links.py push`.
106:Both index systems (per-folder `index.html` and OKF `index.md`) were retired on 2026-08-27 and their pre-commit hook blocks were removed. Never regenerate either; `SCRIPTS/index/README.md` records why. The two hand-made `index.html` pages under `LIBRARY/Resources/GTM Engineering Automations/` are the only ones that remain, on purpose.
112:`0_IDEAS` → `1_DRAFTS` → `2_PUBLISHED` → Social Flywheel. The full pipeline (frontmatter schema, SEO checklist, internal-linking model, sitemap SOP, scripts) lives in `SUBSTACK/README.md`, which is the single source of truth. Do not duplicate that detail here.
124:`ABSORB` or `MERGE` means do not start drafting. Say so, name the article that should absorb it, name what that article is missing, and propose the merge. Push back once, then respect his answer. On `WRITE` say nothing about overlap and just get on with it.
128:Full procedure, the pushback script, the calibration probes and the merge workflow live in `.claude/skills/substack-idea-triage/SKILL.md`. Read it before proposing a merge.
130:### Social Flywheel (Content Distribution)
136:| X / Twitter       | SOCIALS/Tweets/               | tweet\_    | `posted` flag  |
137:| LinkedIn post     | SOCIALS/LinkedIn/             | li\_       | folder         |
138:| LinkedIn carousel | SOCIALS/LinkedIn/<post-slug>/ | carousel\_ | folder (HTML)  |
139:| Substack Notes    | SOCIALS/Substack Notes/       | subnotes\_ | `posted` flag  |
141:The flywheel is exactly three channels: LinkedIn, Tweets, Substack Notes. The Shorts channel is retired and lives at `ARCHIVE/Shorts (retired flywheel channel)/`. Never recreate it or emit `shorts_` files. `SOCIALS/YouTube/` is long-form and sits outside the flywheel. Channel hashtags are retired too; the `type:` frontmatter field already identifies the channel.
147:- Carousel HTML goes in `SOCIALS/LinkedIn/<post-slug>/carousel_[slug].html`. The accompanying LinkedIn caption goes in the same post folder as `li_[Title].md`.
150:### Social File Format
156:type: Substack Note | Tweet
170:Every `li_*.md` also carries `posted:`. The folder is still the state machine, so moving a post into `_POSTED` is what marks it done. `python SCRIPTS/socials/coverage.py --drift` reports any post whose file and folder disagree. When you move a post, flip the flag in the same commit.
172:Coverage is a script, never a judgement call: `python SCRIPTS/socials/coverage.py --gaps`. An article can opt out of a channel with `flywheel_skip: linkedin` in its frontmatter, which reports as `SKIP` instead of `MISSING`.
176:A Substack Note and its X post are one idea in two shapes, so they are written from each other rather than from the article twice. Whichever side Atharva approves first is the source, and the other side is regenerated from it. The review desk carries both on one card and one verdict clears both.
178:The rule and the three pair keys live in [SOCIALS/README.md](SOCIALS/README.md). Never restate them anywhere else.

181:- `python SCRIPTS/socials/pair_tweet.py --note "<note>" --show` prints both sides, and `--body-file` writes the new X post. Always use it, because it carries `series` and `sequence` across and a hand edit that drops either one breaks the pair with no error.
182:- An X post whose Note is also a draft rides on that Note's card, so one row holds both sides and one verdict clears both. Open the X tab on its own to read a post alone. `xgate.py` used to enforce this with a stamp and was deleted on 2026-08-31.

226:Scope is the four draft folders: `SUBSTACK/0_IDEAS`, `1_DRAFTS`, `2_PUBLISHED`, and `SOCIALS/`. A README, a CLAUDE.md or a TODO inside those folders is exempt. The gate exits 0 and stays silent whenever Python, the scorer, or the ledger is unavailable, because a gate that fails closed on its own bugs gets deleted in a day.
252:The full Substack article schema, the SEO checklist, and the internal-linking model live in `SUBSTACK/README.md` (the source of truth). The deprecated `publish_date`, `social_flywheel`, and `internal_links` fields are gone, do not reintroduce them. `title`, `subtitle`, and `description` are retired in favour of `seo_title` and `seo_description`, which are each published as both the visible copy and the search-engine copy.
254:Every article in `2_PUBLISHED/` must carry its live Substack post `ID` in frontmatter. This is gated by a pre-commit hook running `python SCRIPTS/substack/check_ids.py --staged`. Backfill with `--fix`. Never move a file into `2_PUBLISHED/` unless it is actually live on Substack.
259:- Social files: `{prefix}_{Exact Blog Title}.md`
271:- `DIGITAL TWIN/`: identity, voice, audience, goals (read before generating any content). Audience.md holds the ICP archetypes, Experience.md the competency pillars, Socials.md the handle index, LinkedIn Profile - Atharva.md the live profile copy
276:- `LIBRARY/Resources/LinkedIn Winning Templates 2026.md`: **the only six shapes a LinkedIn post may take**, all short list posts written for a reader who has never heard of Atharva. Decided 2026-10-09 from the Depost analysis. `li_format.py` blocks a post with no list (`no-list`) or a first line on I, my, we or our (`self-hook`). A post Zernio already holds is rewritten in place with `SCRIPTS/zernio/li_update.py`, never deleted and recreated.
277:- `LIBRARY/Resources/LinkedIn Content Formats - 100 Post Ideas.md`: **the source of truth for format selection on Substack Notes and tweets.** LinkedIn uses the six templates above instead. Every Substack Note and tweet picks a format from here before a word is written. Use the top 10 first, drop to formats 11 through 100 only when nothing in the top 10 fits, and never invent a format. # Zernio posting

One command turns a tweet file in `SOCIALS/Tweets/` into a published post plus a scheduled queue. This is the standard path for X. Do not hand-write a one-off script and do not post through the web UI, because only `post.py` writes the `_sent.tsv` ledger.

LinkedIn posts do not come through `post.py`. They go through `li_draft.py`, which saves each post as a Zernio draft on the personal LinkedIn profile with its image, alt text and first comment. It refuses the AccuKnox organization page, and a draft never publishes by itself. The file's own docstring carries the full usage.

YouTube videos do not come through `post.py` either. They go through the global `youtube-publish` skill (`python ~/.claude/skills/youtube-publish/scripts/yt_publish.py`), which reads a draft from `SOCIALS/YouTube/yt_*.md`, uploads the video and the thumbnail, publishes to `cozy-console`, and updates the title, description, tags and thumbnail of a live video. YouTube cannot replace a published video file, so the cut must be final first. The skill holds the title, thumbnail and description rules.

## LinkedIn State Follows Zernio

Zernio is the source of truth for a LinkedIn post. `li_sync.py` reads every post on the personal profile, joins it to `_li_drafts.tsv` on `post_id`, and moves the vault to match. A published post moves its folder to `_POSTED` and sets `posted: true`. A scheduled post moves from `_WIP` to `_QUEUED`. The review desk reads the folder, so a rebuild shows the new state.

```bash
python SCRIPTS/zernio/li_sync.py --live
```

Without `--live` it reports and moves nothing. It never demotes a post and never deletes one. A post in `_POSTED` that Zernio does not call published prints as `DRIFT`. The ledger path is rewritten after each move, so `li_draft.py` still recognises the file.

## Run it

```bash
python SCRIPTS/zernio/post.py plan "SOCIALS/Tweets/tweet_Your Title.md"
```

`plan` prints the full schedule and sends nothing. Read it, then send:

```bash
python SCRIPTS/zernio/post.py send "SOCIALS/Tweets/tweet_Your Title.md" --live
```

The first post in the file publishes immediately. Every post after it takes the next free slot, three per day, at 10:00, 14:30 and 19:30 IST. The first slot used is the next one still in the future, so a run started at 01:00 fills today and a run started at 20:00 starts tomorrow.

Dry run is the default on every command. Nothing leaves the machine without `--live`.

## Commands

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `plan <file>` | Print the schedule, character counts and image flags. Sends nothing. |
| `send <file> --live` | Publish post 1 now, schedule the rest, append to `_sent.tsv`. |
| `sync-media <file> --live` | Attach images to posts that are **already scheduled**, matched on exact text. |
| `list` | Print the whole Zernio queue with status, time and image flag. |
| `publish <post_id> --live` | Send a scheduled post right now instead of waiting for its slot. |
| `cancel <post_id> --live` | Delete one scheduled post. |
| `schedule <file> --at "YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM" [--every N]` | Schedule at a time you pick, stepping N days per post. Publishes nothing now. |
| `respace --pin <id,id,...>` | Re-space the whole queue onto the slot grid, order kept. Pinned ids hold their time. |

`publish` refuses anything that is not currently scheduled, so it cannot double-post something already live. Publishing early leaves its old slot empty and moves nothing else, so the rest of the queue keeps the times it was given.

Add `--platform youtube` to target another account. The default is `twitter`.

## Picking the time yourself, and fixing an overbooked queue

`send` always publishes post 1 immediately and drops the rest into the next free grid slots. That
is wrong for a post that has to land in one specific slot, so `schedule` takes the time from you.

```bash
python SCRIPTS/zernio/post.py schedule "SOCIALS/Tweets/tweet_Foo.md" --at "2026-08-30 19:30" --live
```

`--every 2` steps two days per post, which is how an every-other-day run out of one file works.
Times are IST and nothing publishes at run time, so a mistake is still cancellable.

`respace` fixes a queue that drifted past the daily cap. It reads every scheduled post, keeps the
order they already had, and packs them into the 3 daily slots from the next free one forward.

```bash
python SCRIPTS/zernio/post.py respace --pin 6a93c599dc6b09eccb067723,6a93c59a48296bd39db70397
```

A pinned id keeps its time and consumes the slot it sits in, so the usual sequence is `schedule`
the new posts at the times they need, then `respace` with those ids pinned. Everything else slides
later and nothing is cancelled.

Behind both is `PUT /v1/posts/{id}`, which Zernio accepts for a draft, scheduled, failed, partial
or cancelled post. Sending only `scheduledFor` leaves the text and the media alone, which is what
makes `respace` safe over a queue that already carries images. Cancel-and-resend would lose them.

## Attaching an image

Add a `media:` line at the end of a post block inside the tweet file, with a path relative to the vault root. An `alt:` line is optional and becomes the accessibility text on X.

```markdown
"direct traffic" is your analytics tool saying "i don't know."

media: META/Attachments/zero-click-marketing-what-data-says/19-dark-social.jpg
alt: Dark social test, five networks all reporting 100% hidden
```

Both lines are stripped before the post goes out, so they never appear in the tweet. The file stays the single source of truth, which means you edit the markdown and re-run rather than clicking through a dashboard.

To add images to a set you already scheduled, add the `media:` lines and run `sync-media`. It matches each post by its exact text, so an edit to the wording breaks the match and the post is reported as `skip (not scheduled)`. Fix the text or cancel and re-send.

## The 7 day limit on images

Uploaded media lands in Zernio's temporary storage and **auto-deletes after 7 days**. A post scheduled further out than that publishes with a dead image link and no warning.

So the rule is: schedule media posts inside a 7 day window. For a longer run, send the posts first and run `sync-media` again a few days before the far-out ones fire.

## Before you send

1. Run the slop scorer on the file. CRIT must reach 0.
2. Run `plan` and read every line. This is the last point where a mistake is free.
3. Check the character counts in the `plan` output. `post.py` refuses to send an X post over 25,000 characters, which is the X Premium+ ceiling. The limit sat at 280 until 2026-08-29, which was the free-tier number and blocked every long post.
4. Confirm the schedule with Atharva. A live send always needs his explicit go-ahead.

## A reply to somebody else's post always fails

Since February 2026, X only accepts an API reply when the original author has @mentioned you or quoted you first. Zernio reports it as `X (Twitter) cannot reply to this post`, and the post sits in the queue as `failed` forever. Retrying changes nothing, because the restriction is on X's side.

A self-reply inside your own post is unaffected, so this never touches a normal send.

The fix is to `cancel` the failed row and post the text standalone, or to reply by hand in the X app. Five rows from 2026-08-27 failed this way, one of them a leftover test probe.

## What cannot be undone

A scheduled post is deletable with `cancel`. A published post is not. Removing a published post needs `POST /v1/posts/{id}/unpublish`, which deletes it from X itself, and `post.py` deliberately does not wrap that. Do it by hand so it stays a decision rather than a flag.

## How it talks to Zernio

The key is `ZERNIO_API_KEY` in `D:\Atharva\NOTES\.env`. Never paste it into a file, a commit or chat output.

Every call shells out to `curl`, because this machine's Python has an expired CA root and `urllib` fails on the Zernio host. Same workaround as `SCRIPTS/substack/`.

Every request carries a unique `x-request-id`. Zernio dedupes on that header for 5 minutes, which is what makes a retry after a network blip safe instead of a double post.

Account IDs are looked up at run time from `/v1/accounts` rather than hard-coded, so reconnecting an account does not break the script.

## Reading the Zernio docs

`WebFetch` on `docs.zernio.com` returns the empty page shell and is useless. Fetch `https://docs.zernio.com/llms.txt` for the page index, then the `.mdx` URLs it lists. The full spec is at `https://docs.zernio.com/api/openapi`, and it is YAML despite the path, so parse it with `yaml.safe_load`.

Platform limits and quirks live in `LIBRARY/Resources/Zernio - Social Media API Reference.md`.

## Bulk Scheduling a Whole Plan

`bulk_schedule.py` sends a plan of many X posts in one run, with a time per row and a self-reply link on some rows. Added 2026-10-02 for the first 246-post queue on `cultist_dev`.

```bash
python SCRIPTS/zernio/bulk_schedule.py plan
python SCRIPTS/zernio/bulk_schedule.py push --live
python SCRIPTS/zernio/bulk_schedule.py sync --live
```

The plan is `INBOX/Reports/X Queue Plan.csv`. Only `status=queued` rows go out, two per day at most, and the tweet file stays the source of truth for text and image. `_x_bulk.tsv` records every post it created, so a second `push` never double posts.

Images expire 7 days after upload. `push` attaches an image only to posts due inside 6 days. Run `sync --live` once a week to attach the images for the next week. Posts with a link reply go out as a two item X thread through `threadItems`, because that is the only way Zernio publishes a self-reply. The upload endpoint rejects files over about 4.5 MB, so the script swaps in the smaller JPG beside a card or downsizes the PNG.
519 SCRIPTS/zernio/post.py

"""Publish and schedule social posts through Zernio.

Reads a tweet markdown file from SOCIALS/Tweets/, publishes the first post now,
and schedules the rest at a fixed number of slots per day.

    python SCRIPTS/zernio/post.py plan "SOCIALS/Tweets/tweet_Foo.md"
    python SCRIPTS/zernio/post.py send "SOCIALS/Tweets/tweet_Foo.md" --live
    python SCRIPTS/zernio/post.py sync-media "SOCIALS/Tweets/tweet_Foo.md" --live
    python SCRIPTS/zernio/post.py list
    python SCRIPTS/zernio/post.py cancel <post_id>

Dry run is the default everywhere. Nothing leaves the machine without --live.
See README.md in this folder for the full SOP.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import mimetypes
import os
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
import uuid
from datetime import datetime, timedelta, timezone
from pathlib import Path

VAULT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
LEDGER = Path(__file__).with_name("_sent.tsv")
API = "https://zernio.com/api/v1"
IST = timezone(timedelta(hours=5, minutes=30))

# Posting slots in IST, applied in order to each day.
SLOTS = [(10, 0), (14, 30), (19, 30)]

# X Premium+ carries 25,000 characters per post. The old 280 was the free tier.
LIMITS = {"twitter": 25000}


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- io


def api_key() -> str:
    for line in (VAULT / ".env").read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines():
        if line.startswith("ZERNIO_API_KEY="):
            return line.split("=", 1)[1].strip()
    sys.exit("ZERNIO_API_KEY is missing from .env")


_CURL = ""


def curl_bin() -> str:
    r"""The path to an HTTP/2 capable curl, resolved once.

    Zernio sits behind a Vercel bot wall that fingerprints the connection.
    Windows ships curl 8.x at System32 built on Schannel with no nghttp2, so it
    speaks only HTTP/1.1 and every request comes back 403 with an
    `X-Vercel-Mitigated: challenge` header and an HTML body. Git ships curl 7.78
    built on OpenSSL with nghttp2, which negotiates HTTP/2 and is served
    normally.

    A bare "curl" is not enough to pick the right one. Windows CreateProcess
    searches System32 before PATH, so subprocess finds the wrong binary even
    when shutil.which reports the Git one. Hence the explicit probe.
    """
    global _CURL
    if _CURL:
        return _CURL
    seen = []
    for cand in (shutil.which("curl"),
                 r"C:\Program Files\Git\mingw64\bin\curl.exe",
                 r"C:\Program Files\Git\usr\bin\curl.exe",
                 "/mingw64/bin/curl", "/usr/bin/curl"):
        if not cand or cand in seen or not Path(cand).exists():
            continue
        seen.append(cand)
        try:
            v = subprocess.run([cand, "--version"], capture_output=True,
                               text=True, timeout=20).stdout
        except (OSError, subprocess.TimeoutExpired):
            continue
        if "nghttp2" in v:
            _CURL = cand
            return _CURL
    # Nothing HTTP/2 capable was found. Fall back so the caller reports the
    # challenge itself, which names the real problem better than dying here.
    _CURL = seen[0] if seen else "curl"
    return _CURL


def challenged(raw: str) -> bool:
    """True when Vercel served its bot wall instead of the API response."""
    return "Vercel Security Checkpoint" in raw or "X-Vercel-Mitigated" in raw


def challenge_exit() -> None:
    sys.exit("Vercel challenged the request, which means curl fell back to "
             f"HTTP/1.1. Resolved curl was {curl_bin()}, and it needs one "
             "built with nghttp2. Read the note in curl_bin().")


def call(method: str, path: str, key: str, body: dict | None = None) -> dict:
    """Shell out to curl, because this machine's Python has an expired CA root."""
    cmd = [curl_bin(), "-s", "-X", method, f"{API}{path}",
           "-H", f"Authorization: Bearer {key}",
           "-H", f"x-request-id: {uuid.uuid4()}"]
    if body is not None:
        cmd += ["-H", "Content-Type: application/json", "-d", json.dumps(body)]
    raw = subprocess.run(cmd, capture_output=True, text=True, encoding="utf-8").stdout
    try:
        return json.loads(raw)
    except json.JSONDecodeError:
        if challenged(raw):
            challenge_exit()
        return {"_error": "unparseable response", "_raw": raw[:400]}


def committed(path: Path) -> bool:
    """True when git tracks the file. Zernio keeps an upload in temporary storage for 7 days,
    so the vault on GitHub must hold the only copy that lasts. Set ZERNIO_ALLOW_UNTRACKED=1
    to upload a throwaway file on purpose."""
    r = subprocess.run(["git", "-C", str(VAULT), "ls-files", "--error-unmatch", str(path)],
                       capture_output=True)
    return r.returncode == 0


def upload(local: Path, key: str) -> str:
    """Push a local file to Zernio and return its public URL."""
    if os.environ.get("ZERNIO_ALLOW_UNTRACKED") != "1" and not committed(local):
        sys.exit(f"{local.name} is not committed to git. Commit and push it first, because Zernio "
                 "holds an upload for 7 days and the repo is the copy that survives losing this PC.")
    if local.stat().st_size > 4_000_000:
        # upload-direct answers FUNCTION_PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE above about 4.5 MB (seen 2026-10-09
        # on a 6.2 MB post video), so larger files take the presigned route: presign, then PUT.
        ctype = mimetypes.guess_type(local.name)[0] or "application/octet-stream"
        pre = call("POST", "/media/presign", key,
                   {"filename": local.name, "contentType": ctype, "size": local.stat().st_size})
        if "uploadUrl" not in pre:
            sys.exit(f"presign failed for {local.name}: {str(pre)[:300]}")
        code = subprocess.run(
            [curl_bin(), "-s", "-o", os.devnull, "-w", "%{http_code}", "-X", "PUT", pre["uploadUrl"],
             "-H", f"Content-Type: {ctype}", "--data-binary", f"@{local}"],
            capture_output=True, text=True, encoding="utf-8").stdout.strip()
        if code != "200":
            sys.exit(f"presigned PUT failed for {local.name}: HTTP {code}")
        return pre["publicUrl"]
    raw = subprocess.run(
        [curl_bin(), "-s", "-X", "POST", f"{API}/media/upload-direct",
         "-H", f"Authorization: Bearer {key}", "-F", f"file=@{local}"],
        capture_output=True, text=True, encoding="utf-8").stdout
    try:
        return json.loads(raw)["url"]
    except (json.JSONDecodeError, KeyError):
        if challenged(raw):
            challenge_exit()
        sys.exit(f"upload failed for {local.name}: {raw[:300]}")


def account_id(key: str, platform: str) -> str:
    for a in call("GET", "/accounts", key).get("accounts", []):
        if a.get("platform") == platform and a.get("enabled"):
            return a["_id"]
    sys.exit(f"no enabled {platform} account connected to Zernio")


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------- parsing


def parse(path: Path) -> list[dict]:
    """Split a tweet file into posts.

    Posts are separated by a line containing only ---. A post may end with
    `media:` and `alt:` lines, which are stripped from the text and attached
    as an image instead.
    """
    body = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8").split("---\n", 2)[2]
    posts = []
    for block in body.split("\n\n---\n\n"):
        block = block.strip()
        if not block:
            continue
        text, media, alt = [], None, None
        for line in block.split("\n"):
            if line.startswith("media:"):
                media = line.split(":", 1)[1].strip()
            elif line.startswith("alt:"):
                alt = line.split(":", 1)[1].strip()
            else:
                text.append(line)
        posts.append({"text": "\n".join(text).strip(), "media": media, "alt": alt})
    return posts


def media_kind(path):
    """Zernio rejects a video sent as type image, so pick the type from the extension."""
    return "video" if str(path).lower().endswith((".mp4", ".mov", ".webm", ".m4v")) else "image"


def media_items(p: dict, key: str) -> list[dict]:
    """One upload per `media:` line. The Nth `alt:` line is the alt text of the Nth image."""
    items = []
    medias = p.get("medias") or ([p["media"]] if p["media"] else [])
    alts = p.get("alts") or ([p["alt"]] if p["alt"] else [])
    for n, m in enumerate(medias):
        item = {"type": media_kind(m), "url": upload(VAULT / m, key)}
        if n < len(alts):
            item["altText"] = alts[n]
        items.append(item)
    return items


def schedule_times(count: int) -> list[datetime]:
    """The next `count` free slots, starting from the next future slot today."""
    now = datetime.now(IST)
    out, day = [], now.date()
    while len(out) < count:
        for hh, mm in SLOTS:
            when = datetime(day.year, day.month, day.day, hh, mm, tzinfo=IST)
            if when > now + timedelta(minutes=5) and len(out) < count:
                out.append(when)
        day += timedelta(days=1)
    return out


def check(posts: list[dict], platform: str) -> None:
    limit = LIMITS.get(platform)
    for i, p in enumerate(posts, 1):
        if limit and len(p["text"]) > limit:
            sys.exit(f"post {i} is {len(p['text'])} chars, over the {platform} limit of {limit}")
        for m in p.get("medias") or ([p["media"]] if p["media"] else []):
            if not (VAULT / m).is_file():
                sys.exit(f"post {i} points at a missing file: {m}")


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------- commands


def cmd_plan(args, key: str) -> list[dict]:
    posts = parse(VAULT / args.file)
    check(posts, args.platform)
    times = schedule_times(len(posts) - 1)
    print(f"{'#':>3}  {'when (IST)':<18} {'chars':>5}  {'img':<3}  text")
    print("-" * 92)
    for i, p in enumerate(posts, 1):
        when = "PUBLISH NOW" if i == 1 else times[i - 2].strftime("%a %d %b %H:%M")
        img = "yes" if p["media"] else "."
        first = p["text"].replace("\n", " ")[:44]
        print(f"{i:>3}  {when:<18} {len(p['text']):>5}  {img:<3}  {first}")
    n_img = sum(1 for p in posts if p["media"])
    print(f"\n{len(posts)} posts, {n_img} with an image, to {args.platform}.")
    return posts


def cmd_send(args, key: str) -> None:
    posts = cmd_plan(args, key)
    if not args.live:
        print("\nDRY RUN. Nothing sent. Add --live to send.")
        return

    acct = account_id(key, args.platform)
    times = schedule_times(len(posts) - 1)
    rows = []
    print("\nSending...\n")
    for i, p in enumerate(posts, 1):
        payload = {"content": p["text"],
                   "platforms": [{"platform": args.platform, "accountId": acct}]}
        if p["media"]:
            payload["mediaItems"] = media_items(p, key)
        if i == 1:
            payload["publishNow"] = True
            label = "published"
        else:
            when = times[i - 2]
            payload["scheduledFor"] = when.astimezone(timezone.utc).strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ")
            payload["timezone"] = "Asia/Kolkata"
            label = when.strftime("%a %d %b %H:%M")
        res = call("POST", "/posts", key, payload)
        post = res.get("post") or res
        pid = post.get("_id")
        url = next((pl.get("platformPostUrl") for pl in post.get("platforms", [])
                    if pl.get("platformPostUrl")), "")
        print(f"  {i:<3} {'ok  ' if pid else 'FAIL'} {label:<18} {pid or json.dumps(res)[:160]} {url}")
        rows.append((str(i), "ok" if pid else "FAIL", pid or "", label, url))

    with LEDGER.open("a", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        if LEDGER.stat().st_size == 0:
            f.write("run\tn\tstatus\tpost_id\twhen\turl\n")
        stamp = datetime.now(IST).strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M")
        for r in rows:
            f.write(stamp + "\t" + "\t".join(r) + "\n")
    print(f"\nLedger: {LEDGER}")


def fetch_posts(key: str, status: str = "") -> list:
    """Every post, all pages. The API returns 100 at a time, newest schedule first, so one
    request misses the near-term posts once the queue holds more than 100."""
    posts, page = [], 1
    while True:
        q = f"/posts?limit=100&page={page}" + (f"&status={status}" if status else "")
        r = call("GET", q, key)
        posts += r.get("posts", [])
        if page >= (r.get("pagination") or {}).get("pages", 1) or not r.get("posts"):
            return posts
        page += 1


def cmd_sync_media(args, key: str) -> None:
    """Attach images to posts that are already scheduled, matched on exact text."""
    posts = parse(VAULT / args.file)
    check(posts, args.platform)
    queued = {p.get("content"): p for p in fetch_posts(key)
              if p.get("status") == "scheduled"}

    todo = [p for p in posts if p["media"] and p["text"] in queued]
    missing = [p for p in posts if p["media"] and p["text"] not in queued]
    for p in missing:
        print(f"  skip (not scheduled): {p['text'][:50]}")
    for p in todo:
        print(f"  {queued[p['text']]['_id']}  <- {Path(p['media']).name}")
    if not args.live:
        print(f"\nDRY RUN. {len(todo)} posts would get an image. Add --live to apply.")
        return

    print()
    for p in todo:
        pid = queued[p["text"]]["_id"]
        item = {"type": media_kind(p["media"]), "url": upload(VAULT / p["media"], key)}
        if p["alt"]:
            item["altText"] = p["alt"]
        res = call("PUT", f"/posts/{pid}", key, {"mediaItems": [item]})
        got = (res.get("post") or res).get("mediaItems") or []
        print(f"  {pid}  {'ok' if got else 'FAIL ' + json.dumps(res)[:160]}")


def cmd_publish(args, key: str) -> None:
    """Send an already-scheduled post right now instead of waiting for its slot."""
    cur = call("GET", f"/posts/{args.post_id}", key)
    cur = cur.get("post") or cur
    if cur.get("status") != "scheduled":
        sys.exit(f"post is {cur.get('status')}, and only a scheduled post can be published early")
    print(f"  {args.post_id}  due {(cur.get('scheduledFor') or '')[:16]}"
          f"  {'img' if cur.get('mediaItems') else '   '}"
          f"  {(cur.get('content') or '')[:50]}")
    if not args.live:
        print("\nDRY RUN. Add --live to publish it now.")
        return
    res = call("PUT", f"/posts/{args.post_id}", key, {"publishNow": True})
    post = res.get("post") or res
    url = next((pl.get("platformPostUrl") for pl in post.get("platforms", [])
                if pl.get("platformPostUrl")), "")
    ok = post.get("status") in ("published", "publishing")
    print(f"\n  {'published' if ok else 'FAILED'}  {url or json.dumps(res)[:200]}")


def cmd_list(args, key: str) -> None:
    posts = fetch_posts(key)
    for p in sorted(posts, key=lambda x: x.get("scheduledFor") or ""):
        when = (p.get("scheduledFor") or "")[:16].replace("T", " ")
        img = "img" if p.get("mediaItems") else "   "
        print(f"{p['_id']}  {p.get('status',''):<10} {when:<17} {img}  "
              f"{(p.get('content') or '')[:46].replace(chr(10),' ')}")
    print(f"\n{len(posts)} posts.")


def cmd_cancel(args, key: str) -> None:
    if not args.live:
        print(f"DRY RUN. Would delete {args.post_id}. Add --live to delete.")
        return
    res = call("DELETE", f"/posts/{args.post_id}", key)
    print(json.dumps(res)[:300])


def _payload(p: dict, acct: str, platform: str, key: str) -> dict:
    payload = {"content": p["text"],
               "platforms": [{"platform": platform, "accountId": acct}]}
    if p["media"]:
        payload["mediaItems"] = media_items(p, key)
    return payload


def cmd_schedule(args, key: str) -> None:
    """Schedule a file's posts at an explicit IST time, stepping by --every days.

    `send` always publishes post 1 immediately and then fills the next free grid
    slots. This one takes the time from you, which is what a fixed evening slot
    on alternating days needs.
    """
    posts = parse(VAULT / args.file)
    check(posts, args.platform)
    start = datetime.strptime(args.at, "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M").replace(tzinfo=IST)
    times = [start + timedelta(days=args.every * i) for i in range(len(posts))]

    print(f"{'#':>3}  {'when (IST)':<18} {'chars':>6}  {'img':<3}  text")
    print("-" * 92)
    for i, (p, when) in enumerate(zip(posts, times), 1):
        first = p["text"][:44].replace(chr(10), " ")
        print(f"{i:>3}  {when.strftime('%a %d %b %H:%M'):<18} {len(p['text']):>6}  "
              f"{'yes' if p['media'] else '.':<3}  {first}")
    if not args.live:
        print()
        print(f"DRY RUN. {len(posts)} posts would be scheduled. Add --live to send.")
        return

    acct = account_id(key, args.platform)
    rows = []
    print()
    for i, (p, when) in enumerate(zip(posts, times), 1):
        payload = _payload(p, acct, args.platform, key)
        payload["scheduledFor"] = when.astimezone(timezone.utc).strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ")
        payload["timezone"] = "Asia/Kolkata"
        res = call("POST", "/posts", key, payload)
        post = res.get("post") or res
        pid = post.get("_id")
        label = when.strftime("%a %d %b %H:%M")
        print(f"  {i:<3} {'ok  ' if pid else 'FAIL'} {label:<18} "
              f"{pid or json.dumps(res)[:160]}")
        rows.append((str(i), "ok" if pid else "FAIL", pid or "", label, ""))

    with LEDGER.open("a", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        stamp = datetime.now(IST).strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M")
        for r in rows:
            f.write(stamp + chr(9) + chr(9).join(r) + chr(10))
    print(f"Ledger: {LEDGER}")


def cmd_respace(args, key: str) -> None:
    """Re-space every scheduled post onto the daily slot grid, order preserved.

    Zernio has no reschedule endpoint of its own, so this rides PUT /posts/{id}
    with only scheduledFor set. That call leaves text and media alone, which is
    what makes it safe over a queue that already carries images.

    A pinned id keeps its time and consumes the slot it sits in. Everything else
    packs into the slots that remain, earliest first, in the order it already had.
    """
    pins = {i.strip() for i in (args.pin or "").split(",") if i.strip()}
    posts = [p for p in fetch_posts(key, "scheduled")
             if p.get("status") == "scheduled"]
    posts.sort(key=lambda x: x.get("scheduledFor") or "")

    taken, movable = set(), []
    for p in posts:
        when = datetime.fromisoformat(p["scheduledFor"].replace("Z", "+00:00")).astimezone(IST)
        if p["_id"] in pins:
            taken.add((when.date(), when.hour, when.minute))
        else:
            movable.append(p)

    now = datetime.now(IST)
    slots, day = [], now.date()
    while len(slots) < len(movable):
        for hh, mm in SLOTS:
            if (day, hh, mm) in taken:
                continue
            when = datetime(day.year, day.month, day.day, hh, mm, tzinfo=IST)
            if when > now + timedelta(minutes=10) and len(slots) < len(movable):
                slots.append(when)
        day += timedelta(days=1)

    moves = [(p, w) for p, w in zip(movable, slots)
             if datetime.fromisoformat(p["scheduledFor"].replace("Z", "+00:00")) != w]
    print(f"{len(posts)} scheduled, {len(pins)} pinned, {len(movable)} movable, "
          f"{len(moves)} change time.")
    print()
    for p, w in moves:
        old = datetime.fromisoformat(p["scheduledFor"].replace("Z", "+00:00")).astimezone(IST)
        first = (p.get("content") or "")[:40].replace(chr(10), " ")
        print(f"  {p['_id']}  {old.strftime('%a %d %b %H:%M')} -> "
              f"{w.strftime('%a %d %b %H:%M')}  {first}")
    if not args.live:
        print()
        print(f"DRY RUN. {len(moves)} posts would move. Add --live to apply.")
        return

    print()
    for p, w in moves:
        body = {"scheduledFor": w.astimezone(timezone.utc).strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ"),
                "timezone": "Asia/Kolkata"}
        res = call("PUT", f"/posts/{p['_id']}", key, body)
        got = ((res.get("post") or res).get("scheduledFor") or "")
        ok = got[:13] == w.astimezone(timezone.utc).strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H")
        print(f"  {p['_id']}  {'ok' if ok else 'FAIL ' + json.dumps(res)[:150]}  "
              f"{w.strftime('%a %d %b %H:%M')}")


def main() -> None:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__,
                                 formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
    sub = ap.add_subparsers(dest="cmd", required=True)
    for name in ("plan", "send", "sync-media"):
        s = sub.add_parser(name)
        s.add_argument("file", help="path to the tweet markdown, relative to the vault root")
        s.add_argument("--platform", default="twitter")
        s.add_argument("--live", action="store_true")
    s = sub.add_parser("schedule")
    s.add_argument("file", help="path to the tweet markdown, relative to the vault root")
    s.add_argument("--at", required=True, help='first slot, IST, as "YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM"')
    s.add_argument("--every", type=int, default=1, help="days between posts (default 1)")
    s.add_argument("--platform", default="twitter")
    s.add_argument("--live", action="store_true")
    s = sub.add_parser("respace")
    s.add_argument("--pin", default="", help="comma-separated post ids that keep their time")
    s.add_argument("--live", action="store_true")
    sub.add_parser("list")
    for name in ("cancel", "publish"):
        s = sub.add_parser(name)
        s.add_argument("post_id")
        s.add_argument("--live", action="store_true")

    args = ap.parse_args()
    key = api_key()
    {"plan": cmd_plan, "send": cmd_send, "sync-media": cmd_sync_media,
     "list": cmd_list, "cancel": cmd_cancel, "publish": cmd_publish,
     "schedule": cmd_schedule, "respace": cmd_respace}[args.cmd](args, key)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

type: Identity Profile
title: "AI Writing Policy"
description: "The central directive for every piece of writing an AI helps produce."
created: 2026-08-14
updated: 2026-08-14
---

# AI Writing Policy

> **Purpose:** This is the top rule for any writing that another person will read. Every other
> writing file sits under it. [Voice](./Voice.md) says how it sounds. [Long-Form Writing
> Rules](./Long-Form%20Writing%20Rules.md) says how it is built. `SCRIPTS/slop/slop_rules.py`
> says what is banned. This file says what the writing is for.
>
> Adapted from Clay's internal AI writing policy, 2026. The principles are theirs. The wording
> and the vault-specific rules are mine.

Good writing moves an idea out of one head and into another head, clearly.

AI models write fluent text. They do not yet write text you can ship without reading it. As the
author, you take the time to confirm that every idea in the piece is an idea you meant to
convey. That includes the structure and the emphasis, because the order of the ideas is what
decides which ones the reader remembers.

Use AI to brainstorm, to draft, and to proofread. Then apply the five principles below.

## 1. Stand behind every sentence

You own each idea and each sentence in the document before you share it. "The AI wrote that
line, ignore it" is not an answer to a reviewer. A reader who finds one sentence you did not
mean starts to doubt the other ones. So read the whole thing as if you typed it, because from
the reader's side you did.

## 2. Writing is thinking

The work of deciding what to emphasise is the work of understanding the topic. Skip it and you
finish with a document and no new knowledge. Specs, status updates and retrospectives are
proof of thought, so the artifact is only half the point. Even when AI helps you think, you
understand the problem better after you review the result line by line.

## 3. Spend more time writing than the reader spends reading

A short prompt that becomes a long document moves the cost onto every reader. They can prompt a
model themselves if they want volume. One person paying a one-time cost to cut and sharpen
saves every reader a repeated cost. That trade is always worth it.

## 4. Longer is not better

Length is the easiest thing for a model to add and the hardest thing for a reader to forgive.
A long document hides the real content inside sentences that say nothing. When the piece came
from a short prompt, ask whether the prompt itself is the better artifact.

There is no lossless way to expand natural language. Every rewrite changes the meaning, and the
thing doing the rewrite does not hold your actual intent. Readers want your thoughts, even
rough. Polish that costs information is a bad trade.

## 5. Mark raw AI output as raw

You can quote AI text that fails these standards, as long as you label it. "Claude suggested
this, do you think it is worth a look?" is honest and useful. Passing it off as your own
finished thought is what this policy exists to stop.

## How this gets enforced

1. Read the piece end to end before you send it. No exceptions for short pieces.
2. Run `python SCRIPTS/slop/score.py "<file>"` and take CRIT to 0.
3. Cut the document until every paragraph earns its place. Cutting beats adding.
4. When you cannot defend a sentence, delete it rather than rewrite it.

The scorer catches the words. This file catches the reason. A piece can score 0 and still break
this policy, because a clean sentence you did not mean to write is still a sentence you did not
mean to write.

## Related

- [Write Simply](./core/write-simply.md) turns principles 2, 3 and 4 into a working method. It
  carries the plain-style rules, and the test that a sentence which reads badly usually means the
  idea under it is wrong. Always loaded, so it applies to every draft.
- [Runtime contract](./core/runtime-contract.md), the load order (the sequence rule files load in) and the checks.

title: "World"
description: "The villain, the vision, the reader and the owned vocabulary. What every piece of writing is for."
created: 2026-08-25
updated: 2026-08-25

# World

Three files decide how the writing sounds. This one decides what it is for. Every article, post, Note and tweet moves one reader one step away from the villain and toward the vision. A piece that does neither has no reason to exist.

Derived from 80 published articles, 145 posted LinkedIn posts and 53 tweets. The evidence sits in [Brand World Derivation 2026-08-25](../INBOX/Reports/Brand%20World%20Derivation%202026-08-25.md).

## The villain: rented work

Rented work is work you do not keep. You pay for it in hours or in dollars, it produces a result once, and it leaves nothing behind that works for you tomorrow. The bill arrives again next month and the asset never does.

[Principles](./Principles.md) already stated this rule in 2026-02: rent no platforms. The villain is that rule inverted and applied to the reader's whole week.

Three symptoms a reader recognizes in their own calendar:

1. A weekly report eats 30 minutes every Friday, and it has eaten 30 minutes every Friday for two years.
2. One post reaches 40,000 people, and the next eleven reach 300, because the reach belonged to the platform.
3. A process lives in one person's head, so the process stops when that person takes leave.

The word `compound` appears 108 times across 17 published articles. Rented work is what happens when nothing compounds.

### The main symptom: vibes

In 2026 the fastest way to rent your work is to stop thinking. Copy the prompt, accept the first output, ship it, and repeat forever. The tool got stronger and the operator got weaker, so the output belongs to the vendor. The word `vibe` appears 90 times across 19 published articles, always as a criticism.

## The vision: the owned system

The reader builds the system that does their work. It runs when they are asleep, it improves every time they touch it, and it belongs to them when they change employers. Every hour of work adds to something that was already there.

The proof is the two-week test. A stranger opens the repo, reads no chat history, asks no questions, and keeps the whole operation running for two weeks. Pass that test and the system is owned. Fail it and the system was you.

## The main character

A technical operator between 24 and 35 who already shipped something real. A docs site, a product, a small audience, or a job at a startup that trusted them with scope. They are good at the work and their output still resets every Monday. Nothing they built last quarter does anything for them this quarter.

They watch models absorb the exact tasks they built a career on. They cannot tell whether to go deeper or go wider, so they go faster instead.

## What is at stake

By the end of 2027, most of the tasks in their job description run without them. They either own a system by then, or they compete on speed against a machine. The window is roughly 18 months from 2026-08-25.

## The skill tree

Each pillar in [Content Pillars](./Content%20Pillars.md) teaches part of the escape. A piece of content earns its place by advancing one node.

### Pillar 1, AI and Applied AI

- The reader learns to question a default output instead of shipping it.
- The reader gives an agent memory, so it stops starting from zero.
- The reader encodes judgment into files, so the judgment survives the session.
- The reader builds a gate that refuses bad work, rather than a reminder that asks nicely.

### Pillar 2, DevRel and Technical Writing

- The reader replaces a repeated ritual with a tool they own.
- The reader writes documentation a stranger can follow with no follow-up question.
- The reader restructures code so an agent can work on it safely.
- The reader owns the pipe to every platform they publish on.

### Pillar 3, Growth and Content Systems

- The reader builds distribution once and reuses it, rather than posting into the void.
- The reader refreshes an existing asset before writing a new one.
- The reader measures citations and shares, not impressions.
- The reader runs a content system that ships without the reader present.

## The vocabulary

The list holds eight terms. A term earns its place by appearing in the work already, never by being coined in a strategy document. Counts come from article bodies in `SUBSTACK/2_PUBLISHED/`.

| Term | What it means | Body hits |
|---|---|---|
| Rented work | Work you pay for repeatedly and never own | new, the villain |
| The owned system | A system that runs when you are away | new, the vision |
| The two-week test | A stranger runs your operation for two weeks | new, the proof |
| Compound | Every hour of work adds to yesterday's work | 108 |
| Vibes | Using a tool without thinking about the output | 90 |
| Flywheel | One piece of work that feeds the next piece | 47 |
| Digital twin | Identity files an agent reads to act as you | 15 |
| AI slop | Machine-shaped prose a scorer can measure | 13 |

Three terms are new and five are established. Use the new three until they earn their own counts, then check this table again. Drop `second brain`, because Tiago Forte owns it. `Brutalist efficiency` sits in [Principles](./Principles.md) and appears in zero articles, so either use it or stop listing it.

## How to use this file

1. Name the villain or the vision in the first 100 words of any long-form piece.
2. Name the skill-tree node the piece advances, before you write a line.
3. Use a vocabulary term where a generic word would fit, and never invent a ninth term mid-draft.
4. State the season and beat from the current season file, or say the piece sits outside the season.

A piece that cannot name a node is an idea, not an article. Send it back to `SUBSTACK/0_IDEAS/`.

## Related

- [Content Pillars](./Content%20Pillars.md) holds what the writing is about.
- [Voice](./Voice.md) holds how the writing sounds.
- [Audience](./Audience.md) holds the three personas this file collapses into one character.
- [Season 01](../SUBSTACK/GROWTH%20STRATEGY/Season%2001%20-%20The%20Owned%20System.md) holds the current 13 weeks.

type: Identity Profile
title: "Net New Value"
description: "The bar every post, Note, tweet and article clears before a word is drafted. Non-obvious and tactical, or it does not ship."
created: 2026-09-25
updated: 2026-09-25
---

# Net New Value

> **Purpose:** This file decides whether an idea is worth drafting at all. The other core files
> decide how the draft reads. It loads for every channel: LinkedIn, X, Substack Notes, Substack
> articles and anything else Atharva publishes. Adapted from a creator post Atharva saved on
> 2026-09-25. The two-by-two grid is theirs. The application to this vault is his.

## Only Box 4 Ships, on Every Channel

Every insight sits on two axes. Is it obvious to the reader, or new to them? Is it tactical, so
the reader can act on it today, or is it only an idea?

| | Non-tactical | Tactical |
|---|---|---|
| **Obvious** | Box 1. The reader ignores it. | Box 2. The reader skims it, because it confirms what they believe. |
| **Non-obvious** | Box 3. The reader repeats it to a friend and does nothing. | **Box 4, Net New Value.** The reader saves it and uses it the same day. |

Net New Value means box 4: an insight the reader has not heard, with a step they can take now.

The source uses a sleep coach to show all four boxes. Box 1 is "get more rest". Box 2 is "sleep 8
hours a night". Box 3 is "you build up sleep debt even when you feel fine". Box 4 is the coffee nap.
The reader drinks a coffee, naps for 20 minutes, and wakes up as the caffeine takes effect.

The same grid in Atharva's own field reads like this.

1. Box 1. "Use AI carefully in your writing."
2. Box 2. "Put your writing rules in CLAUDE.md."
3. Box 3. "Most rules in a CLAUDE.md never reach the draft."
4. Box 4. "Put the rule in a PostToolUse hook, a script Claude Code runs after each file write.
   Let it run the scorer and return `decision: block`, so a draft with a CRIT cannot save." This is
   how `.claude/hooks/writing-gate.py` works.

## Run the Test Before the First Line

Write the insight as one sentence before you draft. Then answer three questions in writing.

1. Which box is it in? Say the box number.
2. What does the reader do in the next two minutes because of this piece? Name the exact action.
3. Where have they already heard it? If the answer is "every other account in the niche", it is
   box 1 or box 2, however well it is phrased.

A box 4 insight goes to the channel skill. Anything else gets one upgrade attempt, then it goes back
to the idea bank.

## Upgrade the Box by Adding the Missing Axis

A box below 4 lacks one axis or both. The fix is to add the axis that is missing.

1. Box 3 has the surprise and lacks the step. Add the exact command, number, tool name or order of
   operations that turns the fact into an action.
2. Box 2 has the step and lacks the surprise. Find what Atharva's own build showed that the common
   advice gets wrong, and lead with that.
3. Box 1 lacks both. Cut it. Polish on a box 1 idea produces a well-written post that nobody saves.

A long article can carry box 2 and box 3 material as setup. The headline claim and every section's
claim must still be box 4, or the article is a summary of the field.

## New Packaging Counts, Invented Facts Do Not

The source reports a client who gained 10,000 followers from one post. She learned nothing new for
it. She packaged what she already knew in a form her readers had never seen. So box 4 usually comes
from Atharva's own builds, numbers and mistakes, which no other account has.

The fabrication rule in `core/runtime-contract.md` still holds. Never invent a number, a result or a
step to push an idea into box 4. When the tactical detail is missing, ask Atharva for it or mark the
gap as `[the real step]`.

## Related

- [Runtime contract](./runtime-contract.md), the list of rule files that load for a draft, and their order
- [Post Uniqueness Check](../../LIBRARY/Resources/Post%20Uniqueness%20Check.md), the five questions
  that run after the draft exists
- [World](../World.md), what the piece is for

title: "Voice, Tone & Style Guide"
description: "Specificity & confidence"

# Voice, Tone & Style Guide

> **Purpose:** To ensure all generated content sounds unmistakably like Atharva. See [About](./About.md) for identity and [Principles](./Principles.md) for the underlying philosophy.
>
> **Above this file:** [AI Writing Policy](./AI%20Writing%20Policy.md) is the central directive. It outranks this guide and every rule in `SCRIPTS/slop/slop_rules.py`. Read it first.
>
> **Related:** [[AI Slop Is a Skill Issue -- Bad Inputs Made Bad Outputs Long Before AI|AI Slop Is a Skill Issue]] (the published manifesto on why inputs matter), [Audience](./Audience.md) (who we write for)

## Tonal Attributes

| Attribute      | Description                             | Example                                                                                   |
| :------------- | :-------------------------------------- | :---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Direct**     | No preamble. Cut straight to the value. | _"Stop optimizing your logo. Fix your H1 tag."_                                           |
| **Technical**  | Use precise engineering terminology.    | _"The latency bottleneck is in the edge worker, not the DB."_                             |
| **Analytical** | Skeptical of hype, reliant on numbers.  | _"The graph shows a 20% drop, despite the new UI."_                                       |
| **Witty**      | Occasional dry humor.                   | _"It works on my machine, which is the engineer's equivalent of 'thoughts and prayers'."_ |
| **Empathetic** | Understanding the pain of the builder.  | _"I know, configuring Webpack is hell. Here's a template."_                               |

## The signature

Tone attributes tell a model how to sound polite. This section is the part a reader recognises as
you, and it exists because 79 published articles opened in five different registers and none of them
matched. Added 2026-08-09, see item 17 in `SUBSTACK/TODO.md`. Correct it rather than trusting it,
because it was assembled from the vault and not from a conversation with you.

**Stance.** Write from a position. The authority is quiet and comes from having done the work, so
state the conclusion plainly and let the evidence carry it. Never perform confidence, never posture,
never write to sound clever. The register is a well-read adult explaining something they understand
completely to another adult, which means no slang, no exclamation, and no straining for edge. You
should be able to take any subject, including one outside your field, and hand the reader a better
map than they arrived with. Where you are guessing, say so once and move on.

**The reference layer.** This is the strongest voice signal you have and the most underused. You
think in film, books, games, and startups, so let the analogies come from there instead of from the
generic business shelf. A cinematography choice explains a product decision better than a sports
metaphor does. Two or three per article is a voice, and one per paragraph is a tic. The reference
has to do real explanatory work, because a name dropped for recognition alone is decoration and
reads as showing off. Assume the reader has not seen the film, so make the point land either way.

**Openers make a claim.** The first sentence states something you believe and are about to defend.
It never asks the reader a question, never announces what the article will cover, and never
explains who the article is for. If the opener would survive being printed alone on a card, it
works.

Wrong: "Ever felt like you're living in a dream, even when you're wide awake?"
Wrong: "I created this list to help anyone, especially Gen Z professionals and career-switchers."
Right: "Most startups do not die because they ran out of money. They die because they ran out of
attention."

**The test.** Strip the byline and the topic from any two of your articles. A reader who knows your
work should still place them with the same author. If they cannot, the piece is written in the
voice of its subject rather than in yours.

## Writing Style

**Voice & grammar**
- Use active voice. Right: "Management canceled the meeting." Wrong: "The meeting was canceled."
- Address readers directly with "you" and "your."
- Be direct and concise. Simple language. No fluff.
- Simplify grammar where natural. Example: "yeah we can do that tomorrow."

**Rhythm & flow**
- Vary sentence structures (short, medium, long) to create rhythm. Example: "Stop. Think about what happened. Consider how we might prevent similar issues in the future."
- Mix short punchy sentences with longer explanatory ones.
- Use simple punctuation that keeps readers moving forward.
- Maintain a natural, conversational tone.

**Specificity & confidence**
- Use concrete, specific language. Right: "Let's meet to discuss how to improve this project." Wrong: "Let's touch base to move the needle on this mission-critical deliverable."
- Choose definitive statements over conditionals. Say "this works" not "this might work."
- Avoid marketing language. Right: "Our tool helps you track expenses." Wrong: "Our cutting-edge solution delivers unparalleled results."

## Banned words, phrases, punctuation and style

Defined in `SCRIPTS/slop/slop_rules.py` only, and nowhere else. Check a file with
`python SCRIPTS/slop/score.py "<file>"`. Add a new ban to that file, never to this one.

## Formatting rules, the Atharva style

These are persona and formatting calls that a regex cannot make. The banned lists live in
`slop_rules.py`.

1. Break large blocks of text into bullets or short paragraphs.
2. Bold the key insight so a skimmer catches the value. Outside `SUBSTACK/`, mid-sentence bold is fine. Inside `SUBSTACK/`, bold only a label that opens a line.
3. Give a code example where one applies.
4. Write a header as a conclusive statement. Wrong: "Where they actually break." Right: "The disagreement that matters."
5. Link every source and tool that you name.
6. Use no hyphen inside a compound word. Write "second brain", never "second-brain".
7. Use no hashtags and no emoji, unless I ask for one.
8. Say what a thing does. Never call it "powerful" or "best-in-class".

## "Before & After" Examples

**Before (Generic AI):**
"It is really important to optimize your website for SEO because it helps you get more traffic. There are many tools you can use like Semrush."

**After (Atharva Digital Twin):**
"**SEO is a distribution channel, not a checkbox.** If your LCP (Largest Contentful Paint) is >2.5s, Google penalizes you. Don't guess; use **Semrush** or just check PageSpeed Insights. Fix the speed, then worry about the keywords."

## How to edit my text

1. Keep my ideas, claims, point of view, tense and structure. Change only what breaks a rule.
2. Keep the length close to the original.
3. Invent no fact, story, metric or promise.
4. Output the edited text only. Add no commentary.
5. Stay skeptical. Check a claim before you keep it, because accuracy beats polish.
6. Replace "In a world where" with the change and its result, stated directly.
7. Replace "Most people do X" with one specific observation or with my own tactic.
8. Replace "Stop X. Start Y." with the reason, the condition, or the steps.
9. Keep the response dense. Add an example when it earns its space.
10. Use an informative tone. State the fact without sugar-coating it.

# Write Simply

> **Purpose:** `core/pattern-rules.md` says what to cut. This file says what to aim for, and how
> to tell when a draft got there. Loaded on every writing job, right after the pattern rules.
>
> Distilled from three Paul Graham essays: [Write Simply](https://paulgraham.com/simply.html),
> [Good Writing](https://paulgraham.com/goodwriting.html) and
> [Writes and Write-Nots](https://paulgraham.com/writes.html). The observations are his. The rules
> and the vault wiring are mine.

## 1. Simple is the default, complex is a decision

Use ordinary words and short sentences. Keep the technical term and simplify every word around it.

A complicated sentence written on purpose is a tool. A complicated sentence written by accident is
clumsy. Both look the same on the page, so the writer is the only person who can tell them apart.
Never write one by accident.

This rule also protects a draft. An edit that flattens a deliberate long sentence has broken
something, so read the intent before you cut.

## 2. Every sentence spends the reader's energy

A reader arrives with a fixed amount of attention. Energy spent on your prose is energy that never
reaches your idea.

Most readers quit part way through a long piece. Lower friction means more of them finish. That is
the entire return on an hour of cutting.

Fancy writing moves work onto the reader so the writer looks clever. Do not charge them for that.

**What changed in 2026.** The reader now has a model open in the next tab. Ask it your question and
it answers in four sentences, with no warm-up and no history of the field. That is the piece your
draft competes against, and it costs the reader nothing to switch.
