"""Save LinkedIn posts from the vault as drafts in Zernio, image and first comment attached.

    python SCRIPTS/zernio/li_draft.py "SOCIALS/LinkedIn/_QUEUED/<slug>/li_<Title>.md" ...
    python SCRIPTS/zernio/li_draft.py <files> --live

Dry run is the default. It prints what each draft would carry and sends nothing.
`--live` uploads the image and creates the draft. A draft never publishes, so the
post waits in the Zernio console until Atharva schedules or posts it by hand.

What goes where, read from the post file:
  body           everything after the frontmatter, up to the pinned-comment block
  firstComment   the pinned-comment block, minus its heading. LinkedIn has no API
                 to pin a comment, so pin it by hand in the app after it posts
  image          the `media_asset:` frontmatter path, uploaded to Zernio
  video          `media_video:` (an MP4 from the post-to-video skill) replaces the
                 image when present, as a LinkedIn video post
  document       `media_document:` (a carousel PDF) replaces the image when present,
                 titled by `media_document_title:`

The target is the personal LinkedIn profile. The script refuses to fall back to an
organization page, because the AccuKnox page is connected to the same workspace.

Uploaded media expires from Zernio's temporary storage after 7 days. A draft left
longer than that needs a re-run before it goes out.

`_li_drafts.tsv` beside this file records every draft created, so a second run on
the same file is refused unless `--force` is passed.
"""
import argparse
import re
import sys
from datetime import datetime
from pathlib import Path

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).parent))
import post as z  # noqa: E402

LEDGER = Path(__file__).with_name("_li_drafts.tsv")
LIMIT = 3000
PINNED = re.compile(r"\n-{3,}\s*\n#{1,4}\s*\S*\s*PINNED COMMENT\s*\n", re.I)


def personal_account(key: str) -> str:
    for a in z.call("GET", "/accounts", key).get("accounts", []):
        meta = a.get("metadata") or {}
        if a.get("platform") == "linkedin" and a.get("isActive") and meta.get("accountType") == "personal":
            return a["_id"]
    sys.exit("no personal LinkedIn account is connected to Zernio")


def parse(path: Path) -> dict:
    raw = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    m = re.match(r"^---\n(.*?)\n---\n", raw, re.S)
    if not m:
        sys.exit(f"{path.name}: no frontmatter")
    fm, rest = m.group(1), raw[m.end():]
    parts = PINNED.split(rest, maxsplit=1)
    body = parts[0].strip()
    comment = parts[1].strip() if len(parts) > 1 else ""
    asset = re.search(r'^media_asset:\s*"?([^"\n]*)"?\s*$', fm, re.M)
    media = None
    if asset and asset.group(1).strip():
        tail = asset.group(1).strip()
        tail = tail[tail.index("META/"):] if "META/" in tail else tail
        media = z.VAULT / tail
    alt = re.search(r'^media_alt:\s*"?([^"\n]*)"?\s*$', fm, re.M)
    doc = re.search(r'^media_document:\s*"?([^"\n]*)"?\s*$', fm, re.M)
    title = re.search(r'^media_document_title:\s*"?([^"\n]*)"?\s*$', fm, re.M)
    if doc and doc.group(1).strip():
        tail = doc.group(1).strip()
        media = z.VAULT / (tail[tail.index("META/"):] if "META/" in tail else tail)
    video = re.search(r'^media_video:\s*"?([^"\n]*)"?\s*$', fm, re.M)
    if video and video.group(1).strip():
        # A post video (post-to-video skill) replaces the card as the post's media.
        tail = video.group(1).strip()
        media = z.VAULT / (tail[tail.index("META/"):] if "META/" in tail else tail)
    return {"path": path, "body": body, "comment": comment, "media": media,
            "alt": alt.group(1) if alt else "",
            "doc_title": title.group(1) if title else path.stem[3:]}

def main() -> None:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("files", nargs="+")
    ap.add_argument("--live", action="store_true")
    ap.add_argument("--force", action="store_true", help="draft a file the ledger already holds")
    args = ap.parse_args()

    posts = [parse(Path(f).resolve()) for f in args.files]
    done = ledger()
    bad = False
    for p in posts:
        rel = p["path"].relative_to(z.VAULT).as_posix()
        p["rel"] = rel
        problems = []
        if len(p["body"]) > LIMIT:
            problems.append(f"body {len(p['body'])} chars, over {LIMIT}")
        if re.search(r"https?://", p["body"]):
            problems.append("URL in the body, move it to the pinned comment")
        if not p["comment"]:
            problems.append("no pinned comment")
        if p["media"] and not p["media"].exists():
            problems.append(f"image missing: {p['media']}")
        if p["media"] and p["media"].exists() and not z.committed(p["media"]):
            problems.append("media not committed to git, commit it first")
        if rel in done and not args.force:
            problems.append("already drafted, see _li_drafts.tsv")
        status = "ok" if not problems else "BLOCKED: " + "; ".join(problems)
        bad |= bool(problems)
        img = p["media"].name if p["media"] else "no image"
        print(f"{len(p['body']):5d} chars | {img:40.40s} | {status} | {p['path'].name}")
    if bad:
        sys.exit("fix the blocked files first. Nothing was sent.")
    if not args.live:
        print("\ndry run. Add --live to create the drafts.")
        return

    key = z.api_key()
    acct = personal_account(key)
    new = not LEDGER.exists()
    with LEDGER.open("a", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        if new:
            fh.write("created\tfile\tpost_id\n")
        for p in posts:
            item = {"platform": "linkedin", "accountId": acct,
                    "platformSpecificData": {"firstComment": p["comment"]}}
            body = {"content": p["body"], "isDraft": True, "platforms": [item]}
            if p["media"] and p["media"].suffix.lower() == ".pdf":
                # A carousel goes up as a LinkedIn document post, which carries no image.
                media = {"type": "document", "url": z.upload(p["media"], key), "title": p["doc_title"]}
                item["platformSpecificData"]["documentTitle"] = p["doc_title"]
                body["mediaItems"] = [media]
            elif p["media"]:
                media = {"type": media_type(p["media"]), "url": z.upload(p["media"], key)}
                if p["alt"]:
                    media["altText"] = p["alt"]
                body["mediaItems"] = [media]
            r = z.call("POST", "/posts", key, body)
            pid = (r.get("post") or {}).get("_id") or r.get("_id")
            if not pid:
                print(f"FAILED {p['path'].name}: {str(r)[:300]}")
                continue
            fh.write(f"{datetime.now().isoformat(timespec='seconds')}\t{p['rel']}\t{pid}\n")
            fh.flush()
            print(f"draft {pid}  {p['path'].name}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

`SCRIPTS/socials/li_format.py` blocks the two checkable parts. A post with no list of 3 items or more fails as `no-list`. A first line that opens on I, my, we or our fails as `self-hook`.

## His Own Numbers Point to Short Structured Posts

Depost analyzed 19 posts from the 90 days before 2026-10-08. The posts averaged 17 engagements each, an engagement rate of 0.28% against 5,845 followers.

**What worked.** Three posts beat the average by 2.3 to 2.9 times.

- The KubeArmor AI Security CTF Season 2 recap, 36 reactions and 10 comments.
- The Clay scholarship application, 35 reactions.
- "Every team I talk to has already switched models once", 26 reactions and 11 comments.

Each one named a concrete risk or outcome that a practitioner could answer.

**What failed.** The worst posts led with Atharva's own tools or general AI news.

- "If I were launching a developer tool this month", 0 reactions and 1 comment.
- The Peep Laja reaction post, at 0.2 times the average.
- "Substack shipped an official API" and "Anthropic shipped Fable 5.1", 5 reactions each.

**By format.** Video averaged 21 engagements over 6 posts. Image averaged 16 over 11 posts. Plain text averaged 6 over 2 posts.

**The four recommendations,** in Depost's words, reduced to one line each.

1. Lead with one concrete blocker the reader faces before you name AccuKnox or AgentZ.
2. End with one decision question a practitioner can answer, such as "Which approval step blocks your agent from production?"
3. Tie any AI tool or news post to a specific outcome in the opening line, or skip it.
4. Package each lesson as a short structured post, then as a 6-slide PDF carousel.

## Three Niche Posts Show the Same Shape

Depost picked three posts from the niche as the benchmark. All three are numbered lists with one line per item.

| Author | Reactions | Comments | Shape |
|---|---|---|---|
| [Tom Pestridge](https://www.linkedin.com/feed/update/urn:li:activity:7305203402412642305/) | 65,319 | 1,190 | Template 1, nine concepts |
| [Jason Feifer](https://www.linkedin.com/feed/update/urn:li:ugcPost:7211349580154646529/) | 122,777 | 3,898 | Template 3, two reasons, then two exceptions |
| [Chris Donnelly](https://www.linkedin.com/feed/update/urn:li:activity:7309558802943537153/) | 48,522 | 1,392 | Template 1, a repost of the same nine concepts |

Pestridge opens on a promise of nine concepts the reader "MUST know". Each item is a name and one `↳` line. The close is three short lines of meaning and one question. Donnelly reposted the same list and still passed 48,000 reactions, because the list carries the value without the author.

Feifer opens on a rule with an exception. Two numbered reasons support the rule, and two numbered reasons explain the exception. The lesson closes the post in one line.

## Template 1, the Must-Know List

Use it when the material is a set of ideas, tools or rules the reader can use on their own.

```
[N] [things] every [reader] should know about [topic].

1. [Name]
↳ [What it means for the reader, in one line.]

2. [Name]
↳ [One line.]

(5 to 9 items)

[One line: what to do with the list.]

[One specific question.]
```

## Template 2, Pain Then Fix

Use it when the material solves one problem in steps.

```
[The reader's problem, in their words.]

[What the problem costs them, in one line.]

Here is the fix in [N] steps:

1. [Action as a command]
↳ [Why it works.]

(3 to 6 steps)

[What changes after the last step.]

[One specific question.]
```

## Template 3, Never X Unless Y

Use it when the material pushes back on common advice. It earns the click with a rule, then pays it with two short lists.

```
Never [common move], unless you do it like this.

First, [2 or 3] reasons not to [common move]:

1. [Reason]
2. [Reason]

Here is when it works:

1. [Condition]
2. [Condition]

[The lesson in one line.]

[One specific question.]
```

## Template 4, Mistakes and Their Fixes

Use it when the material is a set of errors the reader is making now.

```
[N] mistakes that [cause the reader's pain]:

1. [Mistake]
↳ Fix: [the fix, as a command]

(3 to 7 items)

[The pattern behind the mistakes, in one line.]

[One specific question.]
```

4 mistakes that make an agent fix look better than it is:

1. Testing on new tasks
↳ Run the old version and the new version on the same tasks, in the same clean container. Anything else measures the tasks.

content.content:
scorer reaches CRIT 0 and before you stamp the draft for the review desk. The scorer
checks the words. This checks the point.

Educational content grows a following fast, because people follow accounts that leave
them with something to use. The trap is that facts are public. Anyone can restate how a
thing works. What makes a post worth following is the frame Atharva wraps around the
fact, not the fact itself.

## The five questions

Run the box test in `DIGITAL TWIN/core/net-new-value.md` before these five. A post outside box 4,
non-obvious and tactical, fails before question 1 applies.

1. **Is the frame his, not just the fact?** A post that only restates a public fact
   ("here is how lead scoring works") is common knowledge. A post earns a follow when it
   adds a name, a number from his own work, or a step order nobody else uses.
2. **Can a reader use it in under two minutes, with no re-reading?** Read the draft once,
   at normal speed, with a stopwatch. If a sentence needs a second pass to parse, cut it
   or split it.
3. **Can the reader act on it without messaging him a question?** Every claim needs the
   detail that makes it usable today: the exact step, the exact number, the exact tool
   name. A post that only gestures at a method fails this test.
4. **Does every hard word carry its meaning on the page?** A term a mid-level reader in
   the field would not know needs a plain definition on first use, or it needs to go.
   Jargon that saves the writer a sentence costs the reader the whole point.
5. **Would this post read the same coming from any other account?** If the answer is
   yes, it is boring by definition, because nothing in it is his. Cut it, or add the one
   detail that only he has: a number from his own build, a mistake he made, a name for
   the pattern.

Two more, worth a fast check but not a kill:

- **Sentence rhythm.** A run of same-length sentences reads as flat even when every rule
  above passes. Vary the length on purpose.
- **The opening line.** If it explains instead of stating a fact or a claim, the reader
  scrolls past before question 1 even applies. Run the opening gate below.

A post that fails question 1 or question 5 does not ship. A post that fails 2, 3, or 4
gets rewritten once, then re-checked.

## The Opening Gate Before the Body

The five questions run after the draft. This runs before it, because the hook is the one
line a reader sees for free and the body can only rescue a reader the hook already kept.
Adapted from the hook-writer, post-brief and voice-firewall skills in The $100K Ghostwriter
(Aryan Mahajan's process), cut to what this vault did not already enforce.

1. **Write 5 openings, one per shape.** Use the channel's own shapes: the pattern interrupts
   for LinkedIn, the tweet shapes for X, the hook patterns for a Note. Each carries a number,
   a name or a moment from his material. Never invent one.
2. **Rank them on three questions.** Clarity: does a stranger know the topic in two seconds?
   Curiosity: can they guess the ending from the visible lines? Honesty: can the body pay it
   off with facts he supplied? Ship the one that clears all three, which is rarely the cleverest.
3. **Cover everything after the opening.** If you can still guess how the post ends, the hook
   answered itself. Withhold the answer and show the cost.
4. **Make line two add a fact.** It stays on line one's subject and never reverses it. If deleting
   it changes nothing, it is repetition, so cut it.
5. **Name the one fact the post rests on.** If a stranger replies "prove it", does it hold?
   If it does not, shrink the claim or cut it. The fix is never better wording.

A claim, never a question, opens every channel. `Voice.md` says so, and `li_format.py` flags a
LinkedIn question hook as `question-hook`.

**In a batch,** run the gate only on posts the fresh-agent review scored under 3.0 on `hook_avg`.
Running it on all of them costs more than it returns.

Three skills link to this file: `write-linkedin-posts`, `substack-notes`, and
`banger-tweets`. Edit the questions here. Never copy them into a skill file.
<!-- DIGITAL TWIN/rules/write-for-one-reader.md -->
# Write for One Reader and One Claim

Name the one reader before you draft, and decide the one claim they carry away. "Load order decides which rule wins" is a claim. "Load order" is a subject.

## Why

A piece for everyone reads as a piece for no one.

<!-- DIGITAL TWIN/rules/opening-earns-the-second-sentence.md -->
# The Opening Earns the Second Sentence

Write the first sentence so the reader wants the second one.

## Why

The first sentence is the only one every reader sees.

<!-- DIGITAL TWIN/rules/each-paragraph-answers-the-last.md -->
# Each Paragraph Answers the Last

Make each paragraph answer a question the paragraph before it raised. Cut or move a paragraph that answers nothing.

## Why

A paragraph that answers nothing is a note, and notes break the thread.

<!-- DIGITAL TWIN/rules/take-a-position-then-its-limit.md -->
# Take a Position, Then State Its Limit

Take a position, then say where it is weak.

## Why

A claim with no limit reads as marketing. The limit is what a practitioner trusts you for.

<!-- DIGITAL TWIN/rules/rewrite-by-cutting.md -->
# Rewrite by Cutting, Not Smoothing

Rewrite by cutting and reordering, never by smoothing.

## Why

Smoothing removes the edges that made the draft yours and leaves prose that reads correct and says less.

<!-- DIGITAL TWIN/rules/read-it-aloud.md -->
# Read It Aloud

Read the draft aloud. Rebuild a sentence you stumble on, because the idea under it is usually wrong.

## Why

The stumble shows the idea is wrong more often than the wording.

---
type: LinkedIn Post
title: Never Trust a Quickstart Because It Worked on Your Laptop
source_blog: none
description: "A quickstart that passes on your laptop can fail for every new user. Run it in a clean container."
created: 2026-10-11
updated: 2026-10-11
posted: false
---

Never trust a quickstart because it worked on your laptop, unless you test it like this.

First, 3 reasons your laptop gives the wrong answer:

1. It already has the tools. A clean python:3.11-slim image ships without git, so a pip install from GitHub fails there.
2. It keeps old packages. The dbt DuckDB guide says jafgen --years 6, and jafgen removed that flag 11 months before the guide shipped.
3. It has your PATH. A fresh shell can install a CLI and still answer "command not found".

Here is when a quickstart test works:

1. Every run starts in a fresh container, with nothing installed.
2. A fix counts only after a second clean container passes every step.

I built FirstRun DocTest to run docs this way at the #neatHack hackathon. On the dbt guide it patched the broken step, and a fresh container passed 9 of 9 run steps. I started with 0 lines of code at Saturday's kickoff and had 95 commits 24 hours later, the hardest I have pushed on one build.

@[neatlogs](urn:li:organization:105668039) traced every run, @[Entire](urn:li:organization:111845019) recorded every coding session, and @[cfo.ai](urn:li:organization:106807285) built the business plan. @[Haimantika Mitra](urn:li:person:lzdsSvee2u), this is the reproducible README test, run by an agent.

Your laptop proves the docs work for you, and a clean container proves they work for a stranger.

Which step in your quickstart has only ever run on a laptop that already had everything?

---
type: LinkedIn Post
title: Four Mistakes That Let Docs Drift From the Code
source_blog: none
description: "Your code changed this week and the docs page about it did not. Four mistakes that let docs drift, and the fix for each."
created: 2026-10-11
updated: 2026-10-11
posted: false
---

Your code changed this week. The docs page about it stayed the same, and nobody got an alert.

4 mistakes that let docs drift from the code:

1. Sorting pages by age
↳ Fix: flag a page when the code under it moves and the page does not. An old page nobody's code touched can still be right.

2. Auditing only the docs folder
↳ Fix: read the git history. Match each commit to the docs pages on its topic.

3. Counting only the pages that exist
↳ Fix: list every user-facing feature from the last 120 days, then check that a page names each one.

4. Paying a model to read every page
↳ Fix: one blobless clone and the commit log do the matching, at $0 in model calls.

I built FirstRun DocAudit to run these checks at the #neatHack hackathon, the same weekend as DocTest. On dbt-core it found 15 stale pages, and 72 of 179 recent features with no docs page. That weekend is my hardest push on one build.

@[neatlogs](urn:li:organization:105668039) traced the runs. @[Akshay Hangloo](urn:li:person:9xTZrcwYYC) and @[Haimantika Mitra](urn:li:person:lzdsSvee2u), this is the quiet rot you both write about, found from git.

A docs page goes stale on the day the code moves, long before a user notices.

Which docs page did your last release change without anyone touching it?

# VERIFY: firstrun-doc-audit

## Output

- Final 16:9: `renders/final.mp4`, 1920x1080, 30 fps, h264 + aac, 57.5 s video (container 57.6 s). VO plus the demo pad bed, mixed to -14.4 LUFS integrated, peak -1.0 dBFS. The pad sits about 20 dB under the voice.
- VO-only render: `renders/vo-only.mp4` (straight from HyperFrames).
- Draft: `renders/draft.mp4` (draft quality, inspected before the final).
- Thumbnail: `renders/thumbnail.png`, 1280x720, built from `scripts/thumb.html` on the live pages-table plate.
- Portrait builds: see "Portrait Versions" below.
- Nothing was committed, uploaded or posted.

## How It Was Made

- HyperFrames 0.7.109 (kit). One template, `scripts/index.src.tpl`, built into `index.html` by `scripts/build.py [L|P45|P916]`. The build injects the VO word timing, so every camera move and ring sits on a spoken word.
- Voice: ElevenLabs `eleven_v4`, voice Brian (`nPczCjzI2devNBz1zQrb`), speed 1.1, one call per beat with timestamps (`audio/tts.py`, `audio/build_timing.py`, `audio/script.json`). Slots 1 and 2 answered 401 quota and billed nothing. Slot 3 served every call. Two passes: the first script ran 60.8 s and was cut. The API reported 46 credits for the second pass (b1 7, b2 4, b3 14, b4 9, b5 9, b6 3) and about 47 for the first pass (b3 to b6 read 14, 9, 10, 3; b1 and b2 were not logged and are estimated at 7 and 4 from the same rate). About 93 credits in all.
- Music: `firstrun-demo/audio/music_bed.wav` (the demo pad), trimmed to 57.5 s, -15 dB, 1.5 s fade in, 3 s fade out, mixed with ffmpeg.
- Plates: captured from the live site https://firstrun.atharvashah.com/doc-audit/ at 2x (1440x900 viewport) with Playwright on 2026-10-11 by `scripts/capture.py`, saved in `assets/plates/`:
  - `public-submitted.png`: public mode, `dbt-labs/dbt-core` typed, "already on the board" step.
  - `private-commands.png`: private mode, `acme/private-repo`, the 3 commands.
  - `board-top.png`: dbt-core health strip and What to Ship Next board.
  - `pages-table.png`: Pages Most Likely Wrong, nav hidden.
  - `drawer-project-flags.png`: the project-flags card drawer (card 10).
  - `drawer-release-notes.png`: Ready for You, Release Notes for v2.0.5 drawer.
  - Also captured, not used: `list-public.png`, `public-typed.png`, `ready-row.png`, `board-full.png`.
- `D:\hack-images` files 33, 34, 44 to 48 and 50 were read. Files 44 to 48 match the live page. Files 33, 34 and 50 show an older layout (34 has a red hand-drawn box). The film uses fresh live plates instead, so every frame matches the page a viewer opens today.
- No partner logos appear, so no logo file was used.

## Checks Run

- `node scripts/preflight.mjs`: pass.
- `npx hyperframes lint`: 0 errors, 1 warning (the drawer plate is used in two scenes).
- `npx hyperframes check`: pass. 22 of 22 text checks pass WCAG AA. The 12 info notes are the camera layers overflowing their clip frames, which is the zoom.
- Silence: `silencedetect` at -40 dB finds no gap over 1.2 s inside the VO. The only silence is the end card hold, 54.4 to 57.5 s.
- Loudness: ebur128 reads -14.4 LUFS, peak -1.0 dBFS.

## Frames Inspected

- Seeked in headless Chromium before rendering, and read: 0.3, 2.5, 6.5, 10.5, 13.2, 15.2, 17.5, 20, 24.5, 29.5, 31.8, 35, 39.5, 42.5, 45, 47.5, 49.5, 53, 56.5 s, then 2.5, 13.2, 16, 17.5, 24.5, 29.5, 31.5 and 0.5, 25 s after fixes.

- Pulled from the encoded final MP4 and read (`verify/finalsheet.jpg`): 1.5, 9.5, 16, 25, 35.5, 43.5, 48.5, 56 s.
- Fixed after inspection:
  - Public and private tags covered the "Get the commands" button. Moved them into a side column with a split plate frame.
  - The health-board tags covered the zoomed strip. Moved them into one row along the plate's lower edge.
  - The board zoom cut the `dbt-labs/dbt-core` title in half. Lowered the camera to show it whole.
  - The stale-chip ring was wider than the chip. Resized it.
  - The opening frame showed the bottom edge of the Ready for You cards. Started the camera lower.
  - The drawer scene opened below the drawer title. Started it at the top.

`website/docs/reference/global-configs/project-flags.md` in the dbt-core audit (docs in dbt-labs/docs.getdbt.com). Last touched 2025-07-14, 453 days before the audit. Since then, 29 commits changed code on its topic. Jev rates it 39% likely wrong. Its newest commit is `3f006b9e3`, "Add dbt-flags feature flag registry and --feature", 2026-10-06.

- **Gates:** slop, clarity and `li_format` are all CRIT 0. The pillar check is ON, and all 4 load-order panels exited 0.
- **Spacing:** each post is at least 60 minutes from 15:00, 18:30, 20:30 and from the others. The 16:00 LinkedIn post is 30 minutes before the X post that was already set for 16:30.
- **Hooks:** the DocTest posts open on "your quickstart broke months ago". The DocAudit posts open on "your code moved. your docs page stayed put". Each post has 1 real number and the line "95 commits a day after kickoff, solo". The DocAudit posts tag only the 2 judges, because no tool logos appear in that video. The full texts are in the 4 committed files.
- **Upload:** I uploaded both videos with `ZERNIO_ALLOW_UNTRACKED=1`, so no video went into the vault. I committed and pushed only the 4 post files.
- **YouTube link:** `post.py` cannot post a self-reply, so post the link as a reply by hand.
